title: Which clothing labels and hangtags does your collection need?
seoTitle: Clothing Labels and Hangtags for Private Label Brands
description: Brief neck labels, size tabs, care information and hangtags as separate items. Check folded dimensions, comfort and destination-specific wording before bulk.
author: BEWE4R team
intro: Start with the information each label must carry and the person who needs to read it. A neck label identifies the brand, a size tab helps a customer select the garment, and a hangtag can explain the collection. Product information that needs to remain with the garment deserves its own review before any artwork is released.

toc.text: Draw the visible label, not just the flat artwork
What happens to the label artwork when you add a new size?
Protect the next order from an old file

bodyHtml:
Draw the visible label, not just the flat artwork

A woven tab folded into the side seam loses part of its width in the fold and seam allowance. Supply both the flat and finished dimensions. Mark the front, reverse, fold direction and stitching line. On a neck label, inspect the reverse against skin and check whether the label remains level when the garment is worn.

ItemDecision to recordPhysical approval
Brand labelWordmark, colour, dimensions and attachmentSewn into the intended seam
Size identificationSize system, wording and positionCorrect size visible on each garment variant
Product informationVerified fibre details and wording for the destinationLegible final artwork and matching finished garment
HangtagFront, back, attachment point and any product codeVisible when the garment is folded and displayed

Who approves the wording?

Use the actual composition supplied for the garment and identify where it will be sold. A brand name or printed hangtag does not resolve every market requirement. For EU sales, the official textile labelling guidance explains fibre composition and language considerations. Check UK guidance separately for a UK launch and have the relevant party review your final label. EU textile labelling guidance · UK textile labelling guidance

Put the whole set together

A neck label and size tab may look good individually but overlap when both are sewn in. Ask for one made-up garment that shows the full label set at once. Compare the size on the garment with the bag sticker and the code on the hangtag. For a size run, check that the artwork distinguishes the genuinely variable field from the fixed brand artwork.

What happens to the label artwork when you add a new size?

Check all the places the customer or warehouse reads a size. A garment can have an embroidered size tab, a hangtag, a bag sticker and an online variant name. Add the new size to the master list first, then test one finished unit against all four. A perfectly printed tag is still wrong if it travels with the wrong garment.

Protect the next order from an old file

Date the artwork, keep an accepted sample and link each label to its style and destination. When composition or market changes, identify which wording requires fresh review. Keep the unchanged logo as a separate asset so it need not be recreated.

BEWE4R’s label gallery shows examples of neck tags, design tags, hangtags and wash labels. Send your label artwork and intended placement.
